nodes.title: The Yuan–Zhang–Zhang Gross–Zagier formula (YZZ Theorem 1.2)
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, B an incoherent quaternion algebra over 𝔸_F with ramification set Σ(B) of odd cardinality and B_∞ totally definite, X the Shimura curve system of B, A a simple abelian variety over F parametrised by X with M = End⁰(A) and π_A = Hom⁰_ξ(X, A), K/F totally imaginary quadratic with a fixed embedding 𝔸_K ↪ B, L ⊇ M a finite extension and χ : K^× \ 𝔸_K^× → L^× of finite order with ω_A · χ|_{𝔸_F^×} = 1. Then, as an identity in L ⊗_ℚ ℂ, for all f1 ∈ π_A and f2 ∈ π_{A^∨}: ⟨P_χ(f1), P_{χ^{-1}}(f2)⟩_{F,L} = ζ_F(2) L'(1/2, π_A, χ) / (4 L(1, η)² L(1, π_A, ad)) · α(f1, f2). Here L(s, π_A, χ) is the base-change Rankin L-function L(s, π_{A,K} ⊗ χ) in the unitary normalisation (centre 1/2), α = ∏_v α_v is the product of the normalised local toric integrals of GZ.4, P_χ denotes probability averaging, the height is relative to F, ζ_F(2), L(s,π_A,χ), L(1,η) and L(1,π_A,ad) are completed L-functions as CST's dictionary requires (CST Lemma 2.3 uses the completed L(1,η); finite parts would change the constant by (2π²)^{[F:ℚ]}; the book's own wording is unverified), and the local measures are the corrected ones. The volume-scaled complex integral is a separate object. The identity is first an equality of the two elements ⟨P_χ(·), P_{χ^{-1}}(·)⟩_L and α of the space Hom_{𝔸_K^×}(π_A ⊗ χ, ℂ) ⊗ Hom_{𝔸_K^×}(π_{A^∨} ⊗ χ^{-1}, ℂ), of dimension at most one; it is proved for factorisable f1, f2 and extended by bilinearity, and no zero pairing is placed in a denominator.
hypotheses: A simple and parametrised by X; χ of finite order; ω_A · χ|_{𝔸_F^×} = 1.

nodes.title: Rational Galois descent of Mordell–Weil spaces
nodes.statement: Let H/K be a finite Galois extension of number fields with group G, and let A/K be an abelian variety. The inclusion of K-rational points induces A(K)⊗ℤℚ ≃ (A(H)⊗ℤℚ)^G. If a field M⊂End⁰_K(A) acts on both point spaces and L/M is a field extension, the comparison is M-linear and commutes with tensoring to L. This gives A(1)=A(K)ℚ⊗_M L for the inverse-character convention of GZ.8. It supplies rational descent only; general Mordell–Weil finite generation remains an RP.1 import and Hermitian positivity for nontrivial χ remains a separate gap.

proofSteps: Ordinary Galois descent for rational points gives A(H)^G=A(K). Define the norm on actual points and tensor it to ℚ; after inclusion it is Σg on the rationalized representation.
An invariant rationalized point may have a lift whose gP−P are torsion. A common multiple kills the finitely many differences, so it comes from A(K) after rationalization.

sourceIssues.printed: Proposition 2.5 defines the finite-place factor γ_v as the volume of U₀(N)_v divided by the volume of U_v.
sourceIssues.correction: γ_v is the volume of U_v divided by the volume of U₀(N)_v, as in Proposition 2.4 and in the definition before Lemma 3.5.
sourceIssues.reason: Formula (2.5) is derived exactly as (2.3): converting ⟨f₁,f₂⟩_U and ⟨φ,φ⟩_{U₀(N)} into Petersson norms introduces Vol(X_{U₀(N)})/Vol(X_U), which is the product of Vol(U_v)/Vol(U₀(N)_v). Proposition 2.4 states this ratio, and the proof of Theorem 1.5 applies (2.5) together with Lemma 3.13, whose γ is Lemma 3.5’s Vol(U)/Vol(U₀(n)) = L(1,1_F)(1−e(R)q⁻¹) (pp.23 and 30). With the printed reciprocal, Theorem 1.5 would acquire the factor γ_v⁻² at every v dividing N.
